title: Dragon Ball Z: Resurrection 'F'
summary: Toei's 2015 feature (93 min, 2015-04-18; Toei Animation's staff page: 原作・脚本・キャラクターデザイン 鳥山明 — his first sole screenplay) under the catalog's one PARALLEL owner (I40). THE TASK'S PREMISE FAILS ON THE FACTS, AND IT CHANGES THE SHAPE OF THIS ROW: there is no later Dragon Ball Super MANGA digest of this film — unlike Battle of Gods (ch 1-4, wave 5), the manga SKIPPED the story, so there are no correspondence chapters to record here and `chapters_adapted` is empty by fact, not by omission. Three independent sources say so. ja-WP's arc list prints the arc as 「フリーザ復活編 ;（漫画：未登場 / アニメ：第19話 - 第27話）」 and its prose 「…その次のシリーズである映画『復活の「F」』を原作とした「フリーザ復活編」はその事件の顛末が解説で語られたのみで省略されている」. Kanzenshuu's Dragon Ball Super manga guide: 'prior to the debut of the Dragon Ball Super manga series, Toyotarō penned a three-chapter introductory manga to the Resurrection ‘F’ movie … it is believed that for this reason the Resurrection ‘F’ story arc that appears in the TV series was omitted from the manga, which instead “charged ahead” to the God of Destruction Champa story arc'. The wiki's Golden Frieza Saga infobox leaves `manga chapters=` EMPTY, and its Resurrection ‘F’ (manga) page states 'the Dragon Ball Super manga by Toyotarou skipped the Golden Frieza Saga entirely with only a brief retelling of the events in Beerus and Champa' — that is ch 5 其之五 ビルスとシャンパ, which follows ch 4 其之四 神と神 directly. WHAT THIS SHELF DOES CARRY IS THE ANIME'S OWN RESTAGING: rows 15-27 are the Resurrection 'F' arc (arcs.ts, kind side_source, ruled 2026-08-28; ja-WP 制作: 「劇場版アニメ2作品『神と神』と『復活の「F」』を原作に用いて、各1クール分ほどのテレビシリーズアニメとして再構成・再制作した「破壊神ビルス編」と「フリーザ復活編」」), and Sean already typed rows 18-21 / 23-27 CANON on adopted{author} (原作・脚本 鳥山明, T26 sitting 2026-09-05). I deliver the standing the task rules — filler, the film is a separate licensed work, not a telling of the run's outline — and flag the one-line fork that follows from those same ruled rows. The position is the substantive correction: 0.51 (an air-date derivation) → 14.5, the film in front of the arc that retells it, the shape you ruled for Battle of Gods at 0.5.

position.why: CORRECTED 0.51 → 14.5. On this owner the film PRECEDES its own retelling: rows 15-27 ARE the Resurrection 'F' arc (arcs.ts, ruled 2026-08-28, kind side_source; ja-WP: 劇場版『復活の「F」』を原作に…テレビシリーズアニメとして再構成・再制作した「フリーザ復活編」), so the film sits directly after the Battle of Gods arc's last row and before the next — ep 14 これがオラのありったけの力だ! 決着!神と神 / 'This Is Every Ounce of Power I Have! The Battle of Gods' Conclusion!' (2015-10-11) and ep 15 勇者サタンよ奇跡を起こせ! 宇宙からの挑戦状!! (2015-10-18), identities joined by title + date across en-WP's episode list and ja-WP's 各話 table (R20). That is exactly the shape Sean ruled for Battle of Gods on this shelf (0.5, ahead of the arc that retells it): a viewer takes the 93-minute film OR the arc, not both for the story's sake. The stored 0.51 is only the air-date derivation (the film predates ep 1 by three months) and it would show a sequel before the story it follows — Battle of Gods sits at 0.5 and its own retelling is rows 1-14. NARROWER ALTERNATIVE, STATED FOR THE SITTING: 17.5. The film's own material starts at row 18 (Sean's side_source list is 18-21, 23-27; rows 15-17 are Toei bridges — arcs.ts), and those bridges precede the film in story time: Vegeta's apprenticeship (16), Pan's birth (17), while the wiki dates the film 'just after Pan is born'. ja-WP's own arc header starts the arc at 19. I deliver the ruled arc boundary, 14.5, for consistency with the BoG row; 17.5 is the finer story seam if you prefer the viewer to keep the bridges.

flags_for_sean: FLAG 1 — THE PREMISE THIS WAVE WAS LAUNCHED WITH IS WRONG, AND IT IS THE MOST USEFUL THING IN THIS FILE. The task says 'on dragon-ball-super the DBS manga's later digest of the film is CORRESPONDENCE on that owner'. There is no digest. The Dragon Ball Super manga goes ch 4 其之四 神と神 → ch 5 其之五 ビルスとシャンパ and never tells the Frieza revival: ja-WP 「（漫画：未登場 / アニメ：第19話 - 第27話）」 and 「その事件の顛末が解説で語られたのみで省略されている」; Kanzenshuu 'omitted from the manga, which instead “charged ahead” to the God of Destruction Champa story arc'; the wiki's Golden Frieza Saga `manga chapters=` is empty. Its only trace in the instrument is EXPOSITION — ch 5's opening (the wiki: 'a brief retelling of the events in Beerus and Champa'; ja-WP cites vol 1 pp. 82-83 for the Super Saiyan Blue naming that the film's events produced) and, per the catalog's own batch-20 record (arcs.ts), a ch 32 flashback. Narration of an outcome is not a telling: no correspondence row, no chapter fields, nothing for the display to print. Battle of Gods (ch 1-4, vol 1) was the opposite case, and pasting its shape here would invent pages that do not exist.

FLAG 2 — THE STANDING IS A ONE-LINE FORK, AND YOUR OWN RULED ROWS ARE ON THE OTHER SIDE OF IT. I deliver FILLER as the task rules: on a parallel owner T30 asks 'from the outline or not', and the Resurrection 'F' arc is not the outline's — arcs.ts types it `side_source` ('another licensed work — a film'), explicitly outside the A-E timeline classes, and no chapter of the instrument carries it. The other reading: under T30 canon is 'the story in ANY official telling', and this story IS in an official telling of this run — rows 18-21 / 23-27, which you typed CANON on adopted{author} (原作・脚本 鳥山明) at the T26 sitting on 2026-09-05; on that reading the film is a B-node and the row is canon with no chapters. TWO THINGS MAKE FILLER THE PRACTICAL ANSWER: (a) validate-extras REFUSES a non-filler standing with an empty chapters_adapted ('canon with no chapters_adapted'), so a canon row here would have to be hand-written past the gate; (b) the manga — the instrument the standing is measured against on an adaptation reading — has nothing of it. Whichever you choose, nothing else in this verdict moves: position 14.5, chapters [], no adoption on the row.

FLAG 3 — NO `adopted` ON THIS ROW, AND THAT IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT. The adoption for this film is already ruled and already lands where it belongs: standing-annotations.ts, dragon-ball-super, T26 — eps 18-21, 23-27, kind adopted, basis author ('鳥山明 wrote the film (原作・脚本)'), Sean 2026-09-05. Stacking a second adoption record on the work row would double-count the same act (the RoF shape the sitting itself set: the act is recorded once, on the rows it makes canon). If you rule the row canon under flag 2, the adoption is still the episodes', not the row's.

FLAG 4 — POSITION: 14.5 DELIVERED, 17.5 THE NARROWER SEAM, 18.5 THE JAPANESE WIKI'S. The three arc boundaries in the wild disagree by design: ours 15-27 (arcs.ts, ruled), the wiki's Golden Frieza Saga infobox 'anime episodes=16-27', ja-WP's header 'アニメ：第19話 - 第27話'. The film's own material begins at row 18 (your side_source list) and rows 15-17 are Toei bridges whose events precede it (Vegeta wins Whis over, ep 16; Pan is born, ep 17 — the wiki dates the film 'just after Pan is born'). 14.5 keeps this row parallel with Battle of Gods at 0.5 (film ahead of the arc that retells it); 17.5 keeps a viewer who takes the film from losing the three bridges. One line either way; 14.5 and 17.5 are both free (this shelf holds 0.5, 96.5, 131.5, 131.51, 131.52) and the move empties 0.51.

FLAG 5 — THE COMICALIZATION TRAP, SPECIFIC TO THIS SHELF. Toyotarou — the Dragon Ball Super manga's own artist — drew a THREE-CHAPTER Resurrection 'F' manga in V-Jump 2015年4月号-6月号 (ja-WP; Kanzenshuu; the wiki: 'Released as a promotion for the movie, it covers the same events as the start of the film, to the point in Goku and Frieza's fight where the two are about to transform'). Same artist, same magazine, same months as the film — and NOT the instrument: the Dragon Ball Super manga's ch 1 begins 2015-06-20 with the Beerus arc. A curator reading 'Toyotarou drew a Resurrection F manga' as correspondence would put phantom chapters on this row; that is the trap this wave's premise walked into.

FLAG 6 — RULE WITH THE OTHER THREE ROWS OF THIS SITTING: dragon-ball-z 20778 → 288.52, dragon-ball-z-kai 20778 → 165.51, dragon-ball-z 5152 (Yo! Son Goku) → 288.5 with the Battle of Gods re-ruling that entails. This shelf is the only one of the three where the film's material is ruled canon at episode level — worth saying out loud in the ledger note so the same title reading 'filler' here and 'canon' on rows 18-27 does not look like a defect.
